title: The extension bits of MOVSX and MOVZX are different
summary: Expand byte 0x80 to 32 bits, MOVSX gets 0xffffff80, MOVZX gets 0x00000080.
applies: 64-bit mode for x86-64; Intel SDM Volume 1 and Volume 2
detail: If the destination is EAX, the upper 32 bits are still zero when observing the entire RAX; it is different when the byte is directly sign extended to RAX.
boundary: Sign extension depends on the highest bit of the source width; looking at the hexadecimal immediate in the disassembly alone does not replace the operand width.
relevance: Explain why signed bytes result in completely different numbers when used in subsequent comparisons or indexes.
